title: Allah is pleased with them, and they with Him.
subtitle: The first ones, and those who follow well

row.title: mutual pleasure
sub: He with them, they with Him

then: After many verses on those who stayed behind, the surah turns to {reward}the foremost{/reward}: the Muhajirin and Ansar. Scholars Ibn Kathir cites said they were those who gave the pledge at Hudaybiyyah, or who prayed toward both qiblahs. Then come {idea}those who followed them with excellence.{/idea}
now: You may feel your faith is second-hand, learned from an app, a parent, a convert friend's story. The verse leaves a place in the circle for {idea}those who followed well{/idea}, long after the first ones. Being late does not lock you out.
old: The great reward was only for the first generation.
new: Following their lead with excellence brings me into the same pleasure.
try: Read about one of the early Companions today and copy one small habit of theirs.

title: You do not know them; We know them.
subtitle: Hypocrisy no one could see, not even the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: know myself
sub: the only file I can read

then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ {idea}used to see them day and night{/idea} without knowing exactly who they were. Qatadah drew a lesson: some people claim to know who is in Paradise and who is in the Fire, yet {trap}do not know their own end.{/trap} You know more about yourself than about anyone else.
now: Someone in the comments says that scholar is a hypocrite, that cousin is going to Hell, that family is not real Muslims. It sounds confident. {idea}The verse says even the Prophet ﷺ was not given that knowledge of everyone.{/idea} Your own heart is the only one you can check.
old: I can usually tell who is sincere and who is fake.
new: Only Allah knows hearts; my job is to examine my own.
try: The next time you want to judge someone's faith, look at your own instead.

title: They admitted it: good deeds mixed with a bad one.
subtitle: Hope for people who are partly good
then: Ibn Kathir says these were believers who stayed away from Tabuk {idea}out of laziness and preferring comfort{/idea}, not doubt. Abu Lubabah and some friends tied themselves to the masjid pillars until the Prophet ﷺ would untie them. When this verse came, {reward}he untied and pardoned them.{/reward} The verse covers all who mix good and bad.
now: You pray, you are kind to your parents, you give. And there is one thing you keep doing that you are not proud of. {reward}The verse is for you.{/reward} Not hiding it, not excusing it, just admitting it to Allah is where the door opens.
old: My bad deed cancels out the good in me.
new: Admitting the bad alongside the good is the start of being forgiven.
try: Tell Allah plainly about one wrong you keep repeating. Ask Him to turn to you.

title: Charity cleans the giver, and a prayer comforts them.
subtitle: What giving does for the one who gives
then: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to take charity {reward}to purify and sanctify{/reward} the givers, and to pray for them. Whenever charity was brought, he would pray for the family who brought it, like {reward}O Allah, bless the family of Abu Awfa.{/reward} Ibn Abbas said his prayer was a mercy for them.
now: You transfer your zakah and close the app. It feels like a bill paid. But giving is also a wash for you: the attachment loosens, the heart lightens. {idea}And when someone thanks you and prays for you, that prayer is a gift back.{/idea}
old: Charity is something I lose for someone else's benefit.
new: Charity cleans and comforts me as much as it helps them.
try: When someone gives to you or helps you today, make a short dua for them out loud.

title: Your charity reaches Allah's Hand first.
subtitle: He accepts both repentance and giving

row.title: raised and grown
sub: like a pony raised with care

then: Ibn Kathir says this verse {idea}encourages repentance and charity{/idea}, each of which erases sins. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah receives charity in His Right Hand and {reward}raises it as one of you raises a young horse, until a bite becomes like Uhud.{/reward} Ibn Masud said charity reaches Allah's Hand before the needy's hand.
now: The few coins in the masjid box. The meal you bought the man outside the station. The small transfer you almost did not bother with. {reward}It does not stay small.{/reward} Allah takes it and raises it, the way you raise something you love.
old: What I can afford to give is too small to matter.
new: Allah accepts even a little and grows it far beyond what I gave.
try: Give something small today, a meal, a few coins, and pair it with a quiet repentance.

title: Do your deeds; they will be seen.
subtitle: Seen by Allah, His Messenger, and the believers
then: Mujahid saw this as a warning to those who defy Allah: their deeds will be shown. Aishah said: if someone's good deeds please you, recite this verse. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}do not be pleased with anyone's deeds until you see how they end{/idea}, for people change in both directions.
now: You are on a good streak: praying on time, reading every day. Or you are in a bad one and feel it is too late. {idea}Neither is the end of your story.{/idea} The verse simply says: keep working, it is all seen.
old: My current streak, good or bad, defines me.
new: What I keep doing to the end is what will be shown.
try: Do one good deed today as if it might be the last thing on your record.

title: Three men left waiting for Allah's decision.
subtitle: When your case is still open
then: Ibn Abbas and others said these were {idea}three Companions{/idea} who stayed behind from Tabuk out of laziness, not doubt. Unlike Abu Lubabah's group, they did not tie themselves up, and their pardon {trap}was delayed.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds: they were at Allah's mercy, and {reward}His mercy comes before His anger.{/reward}
now: You repented, you meant it, and still the guilt has not lifted. No sign, no relief yet. {reward}Waiting is not the same as rejection.{/reward} These three men waited too, and the answer came later in this very surah.
old: If I do not feel forgiven yet, I am not.
new: Waiting for Allah's answer can still end in His mercy.
try: Keep up one sincere act of repentance today even if you do not feel any change yet.

title: A mosque built to harm and divide.
subtitle: When something good-looking is built for bad

picture.label: What they said and what it was

then: A man named Abu Amir turned against the Prophet ﷺ and sought outside help to fight him. He told some hypocrites in Madinah to build a base. They built a mosque {trap}next to the masjid of Quba{/trap} and asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray in it, saying it was for the weak on rainy nights. {idea}Allah testified they were lying.{/idea}
now: A new group in the community, with a nice name and a good cause, but every meeting ends with talk against the other masjid. A project you start partly to outshine someone. {idea}The verse asks what you are really building, and why.{/idea}
old: If it looks religious, the intention must be good.
new: Something can look like worship and still be built to divide.
try: Look at one thing you are involved in. Ask honestly: does it bring people together?

title: A mosque founded on taqwa from the first day.
subtitle: Quba, and people who love to be clean
then: Ibn Kathir says Quba was built {idea}from the first day on taqwa{/idea}, to gather the believers. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}one prayer in Quba is like an Umrah{/reward}, and he used to visit it riding and walking. He asked its people about their purification, which Allah had praised.
now: Maybe it is a small, old prayer room with worn carpets, where the same quiet people come every Fajr and take care with their wudu. Nothing about it trends online. {idea}That is often what a place founded on taqwa looks like.{/idea}
old: The impressive places are where real worship happens.
new: A place built on taqwa, with people who keep themselves clean, is what Allah loves.
try: Make your next wudu slowly and carefully, as someone Allah loves for purifying.

title: Built on taqwa, or on the edge of a crumbling bank.
subtitle: What your life is resting on
then: Ibn Kathir explains that a masjid built on {idea}taqwa and Allah's pleasure{/idea} is not the same as one built to harm and divide. The second was built {trap}on the edge of a steep hole{/trap} that gives way. Jabir said he saw smoke rising from the harmful mosque in the Prophet's ﷺ time.
now: A career built on cutting corners. A friendship built on gossip about others. A marriage built on keeping up appearances. They can stand for years. {trap}Then one day the ground under them gives way.{/trap} The verse asks what you are building on.
old: If it is standing, it must be built well.
new: What lasts is what rests on taqwa, not what looks solid now.
try: Pick one thing you are building, a habit, a plan, a relationship. Check its foundation.

title: What they built kept doubt alive inside them.
subtitle: How a wrong project stays in the heart
then: Ibn Kathir says that because of this awful act, {trap}they inherited hypocrisy in their hearts{/trap}, the way calf worshippers stayed attached to the calf. Many early scholars said {trap}until their hearts are cut{/trap} means until they die. {idea}Allah knows and is wise{/idea} in repaying every deed.
now: Maybe you once helped start a rumor about someone. It is long over, everyone has moved on. But you still feel uneasy around that person, still defensive when it comes up. {idea}What we build against others can keep living in us.{/idea} Turning back sooner is a mercy.
old: Once it is over and done, it no longer affects me.
new: A wrong I built can stay in my heart until I sincerely undo it.
try: Undo one old wrong quietly today: a kind word, an apology, a correction.
